title: Optimize quant kernels: INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant fusion, KV cache & batching improvements
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Improves INT8/FP8 quantized kernels with fused smoothquant+dequant paths, reduces serving p99 latency and increases throughput. Includes scheduler and continuous-batching heuristics to better utilize KV cache and reduce wasted compute. Backwards-compatible - no API changes.
description: Context: Quantized inference on recent open models showed suboptimal throughput when dequantization and per-channel smoothquant scaling were performed as separate kernels. This PR introduces fused paths for smoothquant + dequant for INT8 and FP8 variants, updates kernel selection heuristics, and adjusts scheduler/batcher logic to improve KV cache locality and continuous batching efficiency. Motivation: reduce per-token compute and memory churn, avoid extra global memory reads/writes, and improve GPU occupancy for short sequences. Summary of changes and rationale: - Add fused_dequant_smoothquant INT8/FP8 kernels that apply per-channel scaling and dequantize into the compute path, avoiding an intermediate full-precision writeback. Microbenchmarks show up to 1.18x end-to-end throughput improvement for typical chat workloads and ~8% median latency reduction for short-sequence traffic. - Update kernel selection: runtime now prefers fused kernels when model metadata indicates smoothquant was applied at export or when quantization metadata includes per-channel scales. This avoids regressions for models that do not include smoothquant metadata. - KV cache improvements: kvcache_manager now exposes a cheap hot-path hint so scheduler can colocate requests that will hit the same KV pages, reducing PCIe/GPU memory traffic. - Continuous batching: the continuous_batcher heuristics were adjusted to use a tight latency window for short tails and to prefer batching requests that share KV affinity. This increases average batch utilization for low-concurrency, high-QPS routes. - Scheduler tweaks: added a kvcache-aware scheduling policy that biases small requests to warps with warm KV pages before spilling to cold pools. - Tests and safety: added unit tests for fused kernel correctness, end-to-end perf harness for quantized models, and memory-safety asserts. Also added a fallback dequant-only codepath for older runtimes that don't advertise fused capability. Checklist: [x] Implement fused kernels and validation tests [x] Integrate kernel selection into runtime [x] Add KV cache hinting and scheduler heuristics [x] Add continuous-batching integration and perf harness [x] Run regression benches and snapshot results (ENG-1452) Links: Linear: ENG-1452 (quant perf), ENG-1499 (scheduler); Perf artifacts: internal link to perf dashboard (redwood://perf/341500); Related PRs: pr-312459, pr-214900 for prior quant kernel work.

motivation_summary: Reduce memory traffic and kernel launch overhead by fusing per-channel smoothquant scaling with dequantization; improve KV cache locality and continuous-batching to increase throughput for low-latency chat workloads.
perf_summary: Microbenchmarks: up to 1.18x throughput on typical chat-like workloads; p50 latency down ~6-9% for short sequences. Two-socket PCIe scenario: ~5% reduction in transfers and ~3-4% throughput gain when KV affinity heuristic is enabled.
risk_and_rollout: Risk: kernel correctness edge cases for models without proper metadata. Mitigations: runtime metadata checks, fallback dequant-only path, and gated feature flag (RUNTIME_FUSED_QUANT) that defaults off for older dedicated nodes. Rollout: staged canary across 10% of traffic for dedicated and hosted fleets, monitor perf/regressions for 48h before full rollout.
notes_for_backport: Backport candidate for the 2026-02 stable release branch if teams require quant perf gains on short timelines. Backport requires ensuring kernel capability flags and CI GPU images are available on the older branch.
